stages.title: GEOLOGICAL CONTEXT: PLEISTOCENE, HOLOCENE AND CHANGING LANDSCAPES
stages.terms: FACT: Thar evidence indicates more surface water during much of the Pleistocene and increased mid-Holocene rainfall in some phases.
stages.mechanism: Mains angle: Explain climate as mechanism, not master cause: climate - water/biota - resource distribution - technological and mobility response.
stages.consequence: FACT: The impact of the Toba super-eruption on South Asian populations remains debated.
stages.trap: FACT: Thar evidence indicates more surface water during much of the Pleistocene and increased mid-Holocene rainfall in some phases.
stages.answer: Context: The textbook equation Palaeolithic equals Pleistocene and Mesolithic equals Holocene is a useful first approximation, not a rigid law.

stages.title: HUMAN EVOLUTION AND THE SPARSE INDIAN HOMININ RECORD
stages.terms: Correct: It refers to an archaic human population first identified through remains and DNA from Denisova Cave.
stages.mechanism: Correct: It refers to an archaic human population first identified through remains and DNA from Denisova Cave.
stages.consequence: Context: South Asia has a rich lithic record but a meagre authenticated hominin fossil record.
stages.trap: Biological evolution was branching and reticulate, not a neat ladder.
stages.answer: Human evolution is included only to the extent necessary for Indian prehistory.

stages.title: LITHIC EVIDENCE GRAMMAR: ARTEFACT, CORE, FLAKE, DEBITAGE AND CONTEXT
stages.terms: CURRENT: Retlapalle's published lithic analysis counted cores, flakes, retouched pieces, cortex, scars, platforms and reduction strategies, illustrating how modern prehistory moves beyond naming a few finished tools.
stages.mechanism: CURRENT: Retlapalle's published lithic analysis counted cores, flakes, retouched pieces, cortex, scars, platforms and reduction strategies, illustrating how modern prehistory moves beyond naming a few finished tools.
stages.consequence: Correct: It can establish distribution, but behaviour and chronology require stronger context.
stages.trap: Archaeologists reconstruct procurement, preparation, production, use, repair and discard from cores, flakes, unfinished pieces, hammerstones, waste and use-wear.
stages.answer: A stone tool is the surviving product of a technological sequence.

stages.title: DATING AND ARCHAEOLOGICAL METHODS: BUILDING A DEFENSIBLE CHRONOLOGY
stages.terms: FACT: Rock art can be approached through superimposition, style, associated deposits, pigment/accretion radiocarbon, luminescence and uranium-series methods.
stages.mechanism: FACT: Rock art can be approached through superimposition, style, associated deposits, pigment/accretion radiocarbon, luminescence and uranium-series methods.
stages.consequence: INFERENCE: Precision is not the same as accuracy; a narrow date on the wrong event is misleading.
stages.trap: CURRENT: Tamil Nadu's recent scientific-dating programme and the 2024 Retlapalle study demonstrate the expanding use of luminescence and laboratory analysis in Indian archaeology.
stages.answer: Luminescence methods are therefore especially important because they can date sediment burial or last light exposure, while ESR, uranium-series, palaeomagnetism and potassium-argon address other materials and time depths.

stages.title: LOWER PALAEOLITHIC: ACHEULIAN LANDSCAPES AND LARGE CUTTING TOOLS
stages.terms: Mains angle: Compare textbook chronology with newer site dates, then explain the phase through landscape, manufacture and mobility rather than a list of tools.
stages.mechanism: Mains angle: Compare textbook chronology with newer site dates, then explain the phase through landscape, manufacture and mobility rather than a list of tools.
stages.consequence: FACT: Upinder Singh notes that Palaeolithic tools are widespread but excavated habitation sites are comparatively few.
stages.trap: Correct: The old contrast based on supposed absence of pebble tools has been rejected.
stages.answer: The Lower Palaeolithic is marked by large core and flake tools, especially Acheulian handaxes and cleavers in peninsular India.

stages.title: RAW MATERIALS, FACTORY SITES AND THE ECONOMICS OF STONE
stages.terms: INFERENCE: Raw-material distance can indicate direct procurement, seasonal rounds, exchange or embedded travel; it does not identify one mechanism automatically.
stages.mechanism: Scarcity can produce conservation, resharpening and long-distance procurement.
stages.consequence: Stone was not an undifferentiated resource.
stages.trap: FACT: Mahadaha's microlithic stone had to be transported across the Ganga from Vindhyan sources.
stages.answer: INFERENCE: Raw-material distance can indicate direct procurement, seasonal rounds, exchange or embedded travel; it does not identify one mechanism automatically.

stages.title: ATTIRAMPAKKAM AND THE CHRONOLOGY DEBATE
stages.terms: Attirampakkam in the Kortallaiyar basin is central because multidisciplinary excavation exposed a long fluvial sequence containing Acheulian and Middle Palaeolithic technologies.
stages.mechanism: Attirampakkam in the Kortallaiyar basin is central because multidisciplinary excavation exposed a long fluvial sequence containing Acheulian and Middle Palaeolithic technologies.
stages.consequence: Context: The site does not prove which hominin species made the tools.
stages.trap: METHOD: Do not attach the transition to Homo sapiens without fossil evidence.
stages.answer: Mains angle: Attirampakkam is a model case for how new dates revise periodization without eliminating uncertainty.

stages.title: MIDDLE PALAEOLITHIC: FLAKE INDUSTRIES AND PREPARED-CORE PLANNING
stages.terms: Mains angle: Describe the phase as reorganization of the toolkit, raw-material use and reduction planning, not as a sudden replacement.
stages.mechanism: Correct: It is a prepared-core reduction strategy that produces planned flakes.
stages.consequence: Mains angle: Describe the phase as reorganization of the toolkit, raw-material use and reduction planning, not as a sudden replacement.
stages.trap: Prepared-core methods demonstrate anticipation of the desired blank before the decisive blow, though handaxes and cleavers did not disappear everywhere.
stages.answer: The Middle Palaeolithic shows a shift in balance from large bifaces toward smaller, lighter flake tools.

stages.title: UPPER PALAEOLITHIC: BLADES, BONE TOOLS AND SYMBOLIC EXPANSION
stages.terms: INFERENCE: Symbolic evidence expands, yet does not justify reconstructing a formal religion.
stages.mechanism: Wrong: Upper Palaeolithic means only stone blades.
stages.consequence: INFERENCE: Symbolic evidence expands, yet does not justify reconstructing a formal religion.
stages.trap: INFERENCE: Ornament production implies skill, social communication and non-utilitarian value, but exact identity messages are unknown.
stages.answer: The Upper Palaeolithic is conventionally associated with parallel-sided blades, burins, bone tools, ornaments and more visible symbolic evidence.

stages.title: TECHNOLOGY AS ADAPTATION: CORE TOOLS TO MICROLITHIC COMPOSITES
stages.terms: Heavy and small tools can coexist because they solve different problems.
stages.mechanism: Heavy and small tools can coexist because they solve different problems.
stages.consequence: INFERENCE: Miniaturization can support mobility and task diversity, not merely scarcity of stone.
stages.trap: Correct: Tool size reflects task, raw material and design, not a simple cognitive scale.
stages.answer: It must not be read as a universal ladder of intelligence or a clean replacement sequence.

stages.title: MOBILITY, SETTLEMENT AND SOCIAL LIFE OF PALAEOLITHIC COMMUNITIES
stages.terms: FACT: Bhimbetka and Hunsgi include evidence for long or repeated occupation.
stages.mechanism: INFERENCE: Mobility was a knowledge-intensive adaptation involving routes, seasons and social ties.
stages.consequence: INFERENCE: Reciprocity and sharing are plausible in small mobile groups, but status and gender cannot be reconstructed solely from analogy.
stages.trap: It is not direct evidence for every prehistoric community.
stages.answer: Context: Band society is a cautious ethnographic model: small kin-based groups, reciprocal sharing, flexible leadership and division of labour.

stages.title: SUBSISTENCE AND CLIMATE-ECOLOGY ADAPTATION
stages.terms: Context: Organic evidence preserves unevenly, so lithic function, faunal cut marks, grinding stones, starch/residue, seasonality and environmental proxies must be combined.
stages.mechanism: FACT: Kachchh shell middens preserve discarded shells from food consumption and were dated through AMS carbon-14 research.
stages.consequence: INFERENCE: Resource diversity can support longer residence, but settlement permanence must be demonstrated independently.
stages.trap: Palaeolithic and Mesolithic subsistence was broad and ecologically specific.
stages.answer: Hunting matters, but gathering, fishing, shellfish collection, scavenging, plant processing and small-animal capture may have supplied substantial food.

stages.title: PALAEOLITHIC ART, ORNAMENT AND CULT EVIDENCE
stages.terms: Indian Palaeolithic symbolic evidence includes cupules, engravings, beads, unusual discs, ochre and the debated Baghor I platform.
stages.mechanism: CURRENT: Conservation science and direct/indirect dating remain crucial because claims about 'oldest art' are especially vulnerable to overstatement.
stages.consequence: These finds show non-utilitarian behaviour but do not permit a complete reconstruction of religion.
stages.trap: Continuity with present communities can inspire questions but cannot prove unchanged belief.
stages.answer: Mains angle: Use symbolic evidence to challenge the stereotype of purely utilitarian Stone Age life, while explicitly bounding ritual inference.

stages.title: MESOLITHIC TRANSITION: HOLOCENE ADAPTATION, NOT A SINGLE REVOLUTION
stages.terms: It was neither merely a gap between two important ages nor an automatic farming stage.
stages.mechanism: FACT: The Mesolithic record is larger and more socially detailed than the Indian Palaeolithic record.
stages.consequence: FACT: Pottery is absent at many Mesolithic sites but occurs at some.
stages.trap: INFERENCE: Transition means changing proportions and combinations, not universal replacement.
stages.answer: CURRENT: Recent regional microlithic research in the Lower Ganga Basin treats chronology and ecology together, reinforcing that the Mesolithic is regionally defined.

stages.title: MICROLITHS AND COMPOSITE TECHNOLOGY
stages.terms: Function must be tested through wear, residue, experimental replication and ethnographic comparison.
stages.mechanism: Function must be tested through wear, residue, experimental replication and ethnographic comparison.
stages.consequence: INFERENCE: Bow-and-arrow use is plausible at many sites but should be supported by impact and contextual evidence.
stages.trap: METHOD: Do not date an undated surface microlith merely by typology.
stages.answer: Mains angle: Explain why microliths are a technological system: production + backing + hafting + replaceability + functional diversity.

stages.title: MESOLITHIC SUBSISTENCE, SEDENTARINESS AND DOMESTICATION DEBATES
stages.terms: Thick deposits, huts, heavy grinding stones, commensal species, seasonality evidence and cemeteries can demonstrate repeated or year-round residence without a fully agricultural economy.
stages.mechanism: INFERENCE: Pottery and copper can enter forager communities through interaction.
stages.consequence: Some sites report domesticated animals, pottery or cultivated plants, but identification, stratigraphy and dating are frequently contested.
stages.trap: Thick deposits, huts, heavy grinding stones, commensal species, seasonality evidence and cemeteries can demonstrate repeated or year-round residence without a fully agricultural economy.
stages.answer: FACT: Adamgarh domestication claims are questioned because of uncertain dates and stratigraphy.

stages.title: BURIALS, RITUAL AND SOCIAL ORGANIZATION
stages.terms: Mains angle: Use burials to connect settlement permanence, social memory and ritual while distinguishing evidence from interpretation.
stages.mechanism: CURRENT: The 2026 Ladakh aDNA study is later than the Stone Age, but it illustrates how burials can now be studied through osteology, radiocarbon, kinship and genome-wide data together.
stages.consequence: INFERENCE: Unequal grave goods may signal social difference, but a hereditary hierarchy is not demonstrated.
stages.trap: Burial is an action by survivors, not a transparent portrait of the deceased.
stages.answer: Mains angle: Use burials to connect settlement permanence, social memory and ritual while distinguishing evidence from interpretation.

stages.title: ROCK ART: BHIMBETKA, REGIONAL TRADITIONS AND INTERPRETATION
stages.terms: Mains angle: Bhimbetka should be used as a combined history-art-conservation case: evidence of life, limits of meaning, and heritage-management ethics.
stages.mechanism: Mains angle: Bhimbetka should be used as a combined history-art-conservation case: evidence of life, limits of meaning, and heritage-management ethics.
stages.consequence: INFERENCE: Tourism can improve interpretation and funding but increases touch, moisture, litter and infrastructure risks.
stages.trap: It is an archaeological source, not a picture-book transcript.
stages.answer: Bhimbetka's layered record shows hunting, animals, gathering, food preparation, dance, gendered activities and later historical scenes.

stages.title: MAJOR INDIAN SITES AND REGIONAL TRADITIONS: A TEXT MAP
stages.terms: INFERENCE: Site clusters should be read as regional systems connected by movement and exchange.
stages.mechanism: INFERENCE: Site clusters should be read as regional systems connected by movement and exchange.
stages.consequence: FACT: Isampur is a major manufacturing and habitation centre in the Hunsgi valley.
stages.trap: Mains angle: Use a north-west to south-east map spine and attach one diagnostic phrase to every site.
stages.answer: Indian prehistory is a mosaic of river valleys, plateaus, deserts, coasts, caves and alluvial plains.

stages.title: CONTINUITY AND CHANGE TOWARD THE NEOLITHIC
stages.terms: FACT: Bagor's later Mesolithic phase includes increased plant processing and traces of copper interaction.
stages.mechanism: Correct: Pottery can occur among foragers and may be acquired through contact.
stages.consequence: INFERENCE: The Neolithic threshold is a bundle of processes, not a single invention.
stages.trap: Mesolithic communities could experiment with plant intensification, animal management, pottery, storage and longer residence while continuing to hunt, gather and fish.
stages.answer: Context: Neolithic markers include domesticated plants/animals, cultivation, more settled village life, polished tools and often pottery, but these features do not always arrive together.

stages.title: HISTORIOGRAPHICAL DEBATES, SOURCE LIMITATIONS AND CURRENT RESEARCH
stages.terms: Mains angle: Conclude: Indian prehistory is no longer a single march from crude to refined tools; it is a regionally varied history of adaptation reconstructed through converging but incomplete evidence.
stages.mechanism: Mains angle: Conclude: Indian prehistory is no longer a single march from crude to refined tools; it is a regionally varied history of adaptation reconstructed through converging but incomplete evidence.
stages.consequence: FACT: The 2026 Ladakh study recovered genome-wide data from 10 unique individuals and demonstrates current South Asian aDNA capacity, while remaining chronologically later than this topic.
stages.trap: Tools remain essential, but they are now integrated with geomorphology, palaeoclimate, use-wear, residue, fauna, burials, aDNA and heritage science.
stages.answer: The central historiographical shift is from a typological culture ladder to regional, behavioural and interdisciplinary prehistory.
